_readme: THE DEMO'S COMPOSITION — which apps this box's images compose. Same format as the product's own list
(`extensions/composition.base.json` in the Forge monorepo), and deliberately NOT the same content: this
is an INSTANCE's answer, and the whole point of `image = release × list` is that the two can differ and
both be true.
THIS FILE AND `forge.lock` SAY THE SAME THING TWICE, ON PURPOSE. `forge.lock` carries the list the
images WERE BAKED FROM (the pin); this file is the list this repository MAINTAINS (the intent).
`bin/verify-composition.sh` compares the lock against what the running kernel declares — the third
party in the argument, and the only one that is a fact rather than a claim.
WHY EACH APP IS HERE. Nothing is on this list 'because it exists': an app on a list is welded into the
image, and an app nobody uses is bytes and an attack surface.
· banners            — the Outlet home's banner mosaic, and the text-only announcement bar.
· shelves            — the Outlet's 'Quase de graça' / 'Acabando!' shelves.
· reviews            — the coffee store's review wall, and the review form after an order.
· recommendations    — the coffee PDP's bought-together pairing.
· subscriptions      — the coffee store's whole reason to exist: buy once vs subscribe.
· payment-reference  — the bench's payment provider (test cards, PIX display). A list with NO payment
provider is refused at the act of composing: a box that takes orders it can
never be paid for is not a store.
· payment-mercadopago — the provider the demo actually shows a visitor.
WHAT IS NOT HERE AND STILL RUNS: `demo-gate`. An app that belongs to ONE box is never COMPOSED into an
image — it is MOUNTED, from `./extensions`, through FORGE_EXTENSIONS_DIR. It appears in `forge.lock`
under `extensions`, next to nothing else, because it is the only app this instance wrote for itself.
⚠️ THE COPY IN THE MONOREPO. `infra/fleet/lists/demo-instance.json` over there is this list, so the
`fleet-oven` job can bake `release × THIS list` before a release is offered. Nothing mechanical keeps
the two in step — CI does not cross repositories — so a change here is a change there, by hand, and the
symptom of forgetting is an image baked from a list this box never asked for. `verify-composition.sh`
is what catches it on the box, after the fact.
